title: Corner Shop
intro: Corner Shop lets customers browse products, pay by card and receive parcels. Staff manage stock and refunds through a back office. The system is split into storefront apps, backend services, and data and outside services.

layers.name: Storefront
layers.blurb: Customer shopping and staff management interfaces.
layers.tip: Customers use the web shop; staff manage stock and refunds in the back office.

layers.name: Services
layers.blurb: Authentication, catalog, orders, payments, fulfilment and notifications.
layers.tip: Services combine direct calls with events carried by NATS.

layers.name: Data and outside services
layers.blurb: Persistent catalog data and payment, shipping and email providers.
layers.tip: Postgres keeps products and stock. Stripe, Sendcloud and Postmark provide outside capabilities.

journeys.name: Place and pay for an order
journeys.caption: Checkout creates an order, Stripe processes payment, and a payment event allows confirmation.

steps.note: Checkout sends the cart and address to POST /orders.
Receive accepts the order submission.
Price applies the price list and discount codes.
Reserve calls the Catalog service to hold stock.
The Catalog service handles the stock reservation.
The Order service returns the order id and total.
Checkout requests a payment intent from the Payment service.
The Payment service creates a Stripe PaymentIntent.
Stripe reports successful payment through payment_intent.succeeded.
POST /stripe/webhook receives the Stripe callback.
The Payment service publishes payment.succeeded.
NATS delivers payment.succeeded to the Order service.
Confirm proceeds when the successful payment event arrives.
Keep writes orders and order_lines.
The Order service publishes order.confirmed.
NATS delivers the confirmation to Fulfilment worker and Notifier.

journeys.name: Ship a parcel and notify the customer
journeys.caption: A confirmed order triggers label purchase and a shipment email.

steps.note: NATS carries order.confirmed to the Fulfilment worker.
The worker receives the confirmed order.
The worker buys a shipping label from Sendcloud.
Sendcloud supplies the purchased label.
The worker publishes parcel.shipped.
NATS delivers the shipment event to Notifier.
Notifier receives the parcel shipment event.
Notifier uses the parcel-on-its-way template.
Postmark sends the shipment email.

journeys.name: Send an order confirmation email
journeys.caption: Notifier independently consumes order confirmation and sends an email through Postmark.

steps.note: NATS delivers order.confirmed to Notifier.
Notifier receives the order confirmation.
Notifier uses the order-confirmed template.
Postmark sends the order confirmation email.

journeys.name: Change stock and refresh the shop
journeys.caption: A staff quantity change produces a stock event that refreshes the Web shop cache.

steps.note: Staff change a stock quantity through the Catalog service.
PATCH /stock/:sku handles the quantity change.
The Catalog service publishes stock.changed.
NATS delivers the stock change to the Web shop.
The Web shop refreshes its cache.

journeys.name: Refund an order
journeys.caption: Staff request a Stripe refund, which the Payment service records in its own table.

steps.note: Staff request an order refund.
POST /refunds initiates the Stripe refund.
Stripe processes the refund.
The Payment service writes its refund record without using payment.failed.

unclear: Whether the Order service should hear about refunds is explicitly left open.
The Order service subscribes to payment.failed, but its failure-handling behavior is not described.
The Catalog service's stock reservation endpoint and reservation lifecycle are not specified.
The source names orders, order_lines and refunds tables but does not explicitly identify their database.
The exact ordering between writing order records and publishing order.confirmed is not specified.
Back office, Postgres, Sendcloud API and Postmark have fewer than three documented parts; no additional parts are inferred.
